title: Creamsicle Cupcakes (Orange Vanilla)
description: These cupcakes taste like a creamsicle from your childhood, but a little more grown up. Fresh orange zest and juice go right into the batter, so every bite tastes bright, not artificial.
shortDescription: Soft orange vanilla cupcakes take 25 minutes to prep and 18 minutes to bake, topped with a fresh vanilla cream frosting.

metaDescription: Bake bright orange vanilla creamsicle cupcakes with fresh zest and creamy frosting. Easy recipe, ready in under an hour. Try it today.
ingredients: 1 tsp vanilla bean paste or extract
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat softened butter and sugar together for 2 minutes, until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in orange zest and vanilla.
Alternate adding the flour mix and orange juice plus milk, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until combined.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar one cup at a time, then mix in cream and vanilla until fluffy.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, pipe frosting high with a swirl tip. Top with a curl of orange zest.
tips: Zest your oranges before juicing them. It is much easier that way.
Room temperature eggs and butter blend smoother and give a finer crumb.
If your frosting looks too soft, chill it for 10 minutes before piping.
Do not skip cooling the cupcakes fully. Warm cupcakes melt the frosting.
conclusion: These creamsicle cupcakes bring back that orange popsicle memory, but taste fresh and homemade. Bake a batch for spring parties or any day you want something bright.

faq.question: Can I use bottled orange juice instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Fresh juice tastes brighter and pairs better with the zest. Bottled juice works in a pinch, but the orange flavor will be milder.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: Overmixing after adding the flour is the usual cause. Mix just until you no longer see streaks of flour.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy free?
faq.answer: Swap the butter for a plant based baking stick and use oat milk instead of whole milk. The orange flavor still comes through clearly.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to two days ahead and store them unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost them the day you plan to serve.
